newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier sees 77-78 mln T net grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier sees 77-78 mln T net grain harvest.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told the Federation Council upper house of parliament on Tuesday that Russia's net grain harvest this year would be 77-78 million tonnes.

The forecast, detailed in a copy of Chernomyrdin's speech to parliament, is above the Agriculture Ministry's official forecast of 75-77 million tonnes and far above independent specialists' predictions of around 68 million tonnes.
Chernomyrdin said grain output this year would be enough to cover demand until the next harvest.
He made no mention of imports.
Last year's drought-hit harvest was 63.4 million tonnes, the worst in three decades.
Agriculture specialist Andrei Sizov of the independent SovEcon Ltd has forecast 1996 output at 67-69 million tonnes.
The Centre for Economic Trends, a government-sponsored think-tank, puts the figure at 68-69 million tonnes, but other specialists say producers may be under-reporting output.
The harvest is a sensitive issue in Russia, where a collapse in output on farms has upset producers and led to calls for massive handouts from the government.
